landmarks.name: Aeolis Mons
landmarks.significance: Mound of layered sedimentary rock in the centre of Gale. Not a volcano. Lower strata carry clay, sulfate and iron-oxide spectral signatures from orbit.
landmarks.positionBasis: Feature centre from the IAU gazetteer

landmarks.name: Aeolis Palus
landmarks.significance: Crater-floor plain between the northern wall and the mound. Contains Bradbury Landing.
landmarks.positionBasis: Feature centre from the IAU gazetteer

landmarks.name: Peace Vallis
landmarks.significance: Valley cut through the northern rim that fed an alluvial fan on the crater floor near the landing site.
landmarks.positionBasis: Feature centre from the IAU gazetteer

landmarks.name: Gediz Vallis
landmarks.significance: Canyon on the north-west flank of Aeolis Mons along Curiosity’s later route.
landmarks.positionBasis: Feature centre from the IAU gazetteer

landmarks.name: Farah Vallis
landmarks.significance: Large valley entering the crater through the south-west rim.
landmarks.positionBasis: Feature centre from the IAU gazetteer

landmarks.name: Bradbury Landing
landmarks.significance: Where Curiosity touched down in August 2012. First record of NASA’s waypoint file.
landmarks.source: NASA waypoint file, first record (sol 3, RMC 2_0)
landmarks.positionBasis: First record of NASA’s waypoint file (sol 3)
landmarks.uncertainty: Relative position sub-metre; absolute position tied to the mission basemap (order of 100 m)

landmarks.name: Yellowknife Bay — “John Klein”
landmarks.significance: First drilled sample. Mudstone interpreted as a shallow-lake deposit; the samples contain clay minerals and sulfate salts alongside detrital basaltic minerals.
landmarks.source: Drill sol: Curiosity drill-attempt table (PMC8981195, Table 3) / NASA image captions
landmarks.positionBasis: Rover drive-end position at or before sol 182 (record: sol 173, RMC 10_0). The feature itself is within arm’s reach of the rover.
landmarks.uncertainty: Relative position sub-metre; absolute position tied to the mission basemap (order of 100 m)

landmarks.name: “Cumberland”
landmarks.significance: Second drilled sample, a few metres from John Klein.
landmarks.source: Drill sol: Curiosity drill-attempt table (PMC8981195, Table 3) / NASA image captions
landmarks.positionBasis: Rover drive-end position at or before sol 279 (record: sol 275, RMC 16_0). The feature itself is within arm’s reach of the rover.
landmarks.uncertainty: Relative position sub-metre; absolute position tied to the mission basemap (order of 100 m)

stratUnits.name: Siccar Point group
stratUnits.text: Unconformably overlies the Mount Sharp group.

stratUnits.name: Stimson formation
stratUnits.source: Fraeman et al. 2016; Bennett et al. 2023

stratUnits.name: Mount Sharp group
stratUnits.text: Strata of lower Mount Sharp. Mapped from orbit as seven units, including a phyllosilicate unit, a hematite ridge and a layered sulfate unit.

stratUnits.name: Carolyn Shoemaker formation
stratUnits.text: Defined in Glen Torridon where cross-bedded sandstones record more energetic river settings above the Murray formation.

stratUnits.name: Murray formation
stratUnits.text: Finely laminated lake mudstone with rare cross-bedded sandstone; the lowest exposed strata of the Mount Sharp group.
stratUnits.source: Rampe et al. 2017; Fraeman et al. 2016

stratUnits.name: Bradbury group
stratUnits.text: Strata explored on the crater floor; with the Mount Sharp group, the oldest strata in Gale.
stratUnits.source: Fraeman et al. 2016, citing Grotzinger et al. 2015

stratUnits.name: Yellowknife Bay formation
stratUnits.text: Includes the Sheepbed mudstone member sampled at John Klein and Cumberland.

unitNote: Formations and groups are interpretations. Contacts are known where the rover crossed them and inferred elsewhere. No unit polygons are drawn because no public vector map exists.

D01.name: Mars MSL Gale Merged DEM 1 m (v3)
D01.instrument: HiRISE, CTX (MRO); HRSC (Mars Express); controlled to MOLA
D01.resolutionEffective: 1 m only where HiRISE stereo exists; elsewhere filled from CTX, HRSC or MOLA with no source mask
D01.limitations: Horizontal accuracy about 100 m where HRSC-controlled; about 1 m vertical. Fine-scale slope is conditional on the unknown source at each point.
D01.citation: Calef III, F.J. and Parker, T., 2016, PDS Annex, USGS.
D01.use: Rover-region elevation tiles (prepared locally by scripts/prepare_terrain.py rover).

D02.name: 30-m HRSC DTM Mosaic of Gale Crater
D02.resolutionEffective: Not stated by source; treat as 30 m or coarser
D02.coverage: Gale crater (bounds read from file at preparation time)
D02.limitations: No accuracy assessment on the record. Vertical datum must be checked against D01 before use (scripts/prepare_terrain.py check).
D02.citation: Persaud, D.M., Putri, A.D.R., Muller, J.-P., 2021, Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.5808354 (CC BY 4.0).

D03.name: MGS MOLA – MEX HRSC Blended DEM Global 200 m (v2)
D03.resolutionEffective: 200 m where HRSC DEMs exist; MOLA-interpolated elsewhere
D03.coverage: Global (Gale window clipped at preparation time)
D03.limitations: Interim product; blending artefacts in places; total elevation uncertainty at least ±3 m.
D03.citation: Fergason, R.L., Hare, T.M., Laura, J., 2018, Astrogeology PDS Annex, USGS.

D05.name: MRO CTX Gale Crater Mosaic (Mars Trek layer Gale_CTX_BlockAdj_dd)
D05.resolutionEffective: about 10 m/px at the service maximum (zoom 12)
D05.limitations: Greyscale. A mosaic of images taken on different dates and lighting. Registration against the elevation data has not yet been measured.
D05.citation: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS; served by NASA Solar System Treks.

D06.name: MRO HiRISE Curiosity Roving Site Mosaic (Mars Trek layer curiosity_hirise_mosaic)
D06.resolutionEffective: about 0.64 m/px at the service maximum (zoom 16)
D06.limitations: Greyscale. Covers the rover corridor only.
D06.citation: NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona; served by NASA Solar System Treks.
D06.use: Close-range surface texture inside its footprint.

D12.name: Curiosity drive-end waypoints (MSL_waypoints.json)
D12.resolutionEffective: Relative positions sub-metre; absolute position tied to the mission basemap (order of 100 m)
D12.coverage: Bradbury Landing to the current position
D12.limitations: Undocumented endpoint behind NASA’s location map. Not every sol has a record.
D12.use: Waypoints, position by sol, odometry, landmark positions.

D13.name: Curiosity traverse path (MSL_traverse.json)
D13.limitations: Features carry no sol attribute; MarsWalk joins the path to waypoints by position.

D21.name: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature
D21.resolutionEffective: Extents are approximate (stated by the gazetteer)
D21.citation: Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, IAU / USGS Astrogeology.

D22.name: Curiosity REMS daily summary feed
D22.resolutionNative: One record per sol, at the rover
D22.coverage: The rover’s position on each sol
D22.limitations: Calibrated wind does not exist (sensor damaged at landing). Humidity is not reported in the feed. The feed may lag.
D22.use: Observed daily temperature, pressure and UV at the rover.

unavailableLayers.name: CRISM spectral parameters (clay, sulfate, hematite indicators)
unavailableLayers.reason: Needs per-observation spectral processing of PDS cubes (registry D18). Not built.

unavailableLayers.name: Geological unit polygons
unavailableLayers.reason: No public GIS files exist for the published map (registry D16). Unit glossary only.

unavailableLayers.name: THEMIS thermal inertia (100 m)
unavailableLayers.reason: The USGS tile covering Gale has not been located (registry D19b).

unavailableLayers.name: Modelled atmosphere (Mars Climate Database)
unavailableLayers.reason: Requires registration and an offline run (registry D24). Not built.

unavailableLayers.name: Natural-colour imagery
unavailableLayers.reason: No verified crater-wide colour dataset exists (gap G1).

Derived.note: Computed from measurements by a documented method

Interpreted.note: Scientific judgement about what the data mean

galeConfig.name: Gale Crater

weather.sourceNote: Measured by REMS on Curiosity itself, so they describe one point in Gale, not the whole crater.
weather.windNote: Wind has no calibrated speed or direction: the sensor was damaged early in the mission.
weather.archiveNote: The public daily feed has no record for this sol. Older sols are in the PDS REMS archive, which is not integrated.

geology.note: Formations and groups are interpretations. Contacts are known where the rover crossed them and inferred elsewhere. No unit polygons are drawn because no public vector map exists.
geology.intro: The rocks Curiosity drives over are grouped into units — bodies of rock that formed in the same way at roughly the same time. These descriptions come from published mapping, not from a data layer.
geology.polygonsLockNote: No public GIS files exist for the published map
geology.polygonsNote: Gale’s geological map was published as a figure, not as data, so there is no unit layer to draw here. The written unit descriptions are in the Geology section of the inspector.

galeConfig.overview: An impact crater 154 km across with a mound of layered rock at its centre, Aeolis Mons. NASA’s Curiosity rover landed on the northern floor in 2012 and has been climbing the mound ever since.
galeConfig.playNote: Astronaut exploration, missions, sample collection and science notebook are planned for the next phase. The scientific MAP workspace is available now.
